registrar_rulings.reason: The food is already priced: commodities.json carries weekly id chuck-roast (label 'Chuck Roast', unit lb, include 'chuck roast'/'chuck pot roast'/'beef chuck\b'), it is live in smp-feed.json, and the recipe board carries it as beef-chuck-roast with six whole-roast rows ($6.64-$10.99/lb, cheapest Sam's $7.47) which recipe-floor-id-map already routes via 'beef-chuck-roast' -> 'chuck-roast'. Stewing beef is cubed chuck - same food, same lb unit; the pre-cut tray is the same food at a convenience premium, so minting stew-beef would put one food under two ids at deliberately disagreeing prices (the panko failure mode), and its include patterns ('stew meat', 'beef for stew ... chuck') would collide with chuck-roast's 'beef chuck\b' in the daily dupe audit - note canned beef-stew already excludes 'stew meat' precisely to route it to the meat id. FOLLOW-UP EDITS: (1) add alias pair 'stew-beef' -> 'chuck-roast' (and/or the recipe spelling 'stewing-beef') to recipe-floor-id-map.json via the sanctioned editor; (2) SEPARATE NAME RULING - ingredients.json has no 'stewing beef' row (nearest vocab rows are the two ground beefs, a different form), so add the vocabulary NAME 'stewing beef' resolving to the Beef Chuck Roast food-macros row; the name row must not mint an id. If Brad later wants the tray SKU tracked as its own price class, that is a new deliberate-variant proposal (stew-meat + allowlist pair vs chuck-roast) requiring its own ~150-pattern exclude list, not this recipe's blocker.
